commits.message:
A control inside a sequence runs in the tokenizer, after any string the sequence cuts off; a C0 break there ends the line and carries the sequence on (rich-control-codes-xh4n.8qs)

Replaces the executedFirst text rewrite, which moved a BEL or FF into a cut-off
string's payload. decodeLine now follows the rule too, and LF joins VT and FF.
Sequence patterns come from one builder; RUN_IN_SEQUENCE derives from ABORTS.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
A C0 control inside a CSI or an escape runs ahead of it and the sequence goes on, as a VT500 parser does (rich-control-codes-xh4n.8qs)

A string escape's payload, an OSC 8 URI included, ends at CAN or SUB as a terminal's parser aborts it (rich-control-codes-xh4n.52p) (#588)

* A string escape's payload, an OSC 8 URI included, ends at CAN or SUB as a terminal's parser aborts it (rich-control-codes-xh4n.52p)

* CAN and SUB abort a CSI or an escape's intermediates as they do a string: one ABORTS set (rich-control-codes-xh4n.52p)

* A string escape CAN or SUB aborts is silent, as an aborted CSI is (rich-control-codes-xh4n.52p)

* An ST with no string to end is inert, as the one a CAN or SUB leaves; one prefix per sequence so far (rich-control-codes-xh4n.52p)

* Say why performed never sees an abort from beyond its bytes (rich-control-codes-xh4n.52p)
De-emphasized widget text is drawn in foreground-muted, held to its 3:1 floor, not terminal dim (rich-unfiled-791c.yyzs)
